summary.text: A 55-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes on canagliflozin 300 mg daily developed nausea, vomiting and polyuria over 24 hours, with tachycardia, hypotension, dry mucous membranes and epigastric abdominal pain.

After acute gastrointestinal illness she was diagnosed with canagliflozin-associated diabetic ketoacidosis based on a serum beta hydroxybutyrate of 12.43 mmol/L, with acidosis (anion gap 32 mmol/L) and acute kidney injury; acute pancreatitis was suggested. Her serum glucose was 366 mg/dL. Table 1 reports serial electrolytes, renal function, glucose and venous blood gas values at 0, 3, 6.5, 10 and 12 hours after presentation.

She received continuous insulin infusion and intravenous normal saline resuscitation; in the intensive care unit her anion gap normalized, with resolution of ketosis and acidosis. She was transitioned to metformin and glipizide and discharged home on hospital day 3.

summary.text: A 54-year-old man with type 1 diabetes on Humalog insulin, albiglutide 50 mg and canagliflozin 300 mg PO daily developed abdominal pain, nausea and vomiting, with tachycardia, tachypnea, dry mucous membranes and epigastric tenderness.

After acute gastrointestinal illness, laboratory analysis showed acidosis with an elevated anion gap of 27 mmol/L; a beta hydroxybutyrate of 15.35 mmol/L with glucose 327 mg/dL led to a diagnosis of canagliflozin-associated diabetic ketoacidosis. Table 1 reports serial electrolytes, renal function, glucose and venous blood gas values at 0, 2.5, 5, 8 and 14 hours after presentation.

He underwent volume resuscitation and an intravenous insulin infusion until the anion gap had normalized, with resolution of ketosis and acidosis; he improved and returned home after 3 days of hospitalization.
